architecture_principles: physical discovery comes before candidate ranking
the Agent uses measured rheological regularities as scientific tools rather than optimizing benchmark recovery
state-aware rheology, external chemistry evidence and process uncertainty serve distinct scientific roles
candidate selection should maximize usefulness and interpretability for the observed material failure mode
deterministic calculations are separated from language-model judgment
the Skeptic and Robustness Adjudicator are decision-quality controls, not components that need ablation to justify their existence
the final recommendation is frozen before physical adjudication
only concise auditable outputs are stored; hidden chain-of-thought is not scientific evidence
held-out result data are structurally removed before outcome-blind preexperimental reconstruction payloads are assembled
external analogue percentages define supported regions, not exact local optima
performance mitigation and causal isolation are distinct experiment intents; single-factor attribution is not the universal default
among similarly supported candidates, the minimum sufficient intervention is preferred
architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> evidence/tool layer -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze
architecture.claim_boundary: V3.4.0 is an outcome-blind reconstruction of the preexperimental decision state using only evidence available before the validation result. It may support recovery of the scientific problem, intervention family, and formulation neighborhood, but it must not be described as a recovered contemporaneous machine record or as proof that the exact historical recipe was independently predicted.

non_goals: proving that every internal Agent module is individually necessary through ablation
making architecture benchmarking the main scientific contribution
optimizing held-out-region recovery as the main objective
claiming that literature-prior proximity predicts the wet-lab outcome
replacing the material-science result with an LLM-systems paper

architecture.purpose: Outcome-blind scientific decision Agent that reconstructs the preexperimental decision state: it extracts material-response regularities from measured PUR rheology, selects an intervention strategy, and freezes one useful formulation-process experiment point without access to the later validation formulation or outcome.
required_scientific_sequence: state the positive material regularities and their boundaries
translate those regularities into a design objective
use external evidence to identify chemically plausible intervention directions
adjudicate robustness to reasonable alternative evidence interpretations
freeze one useful experiment point and a falsifiable measurement criterion
architecture.secondary_replay_role: Deprecated for the current study narrative. The active Stage-1 evaluation is a single outcome-blind preexperimental reconstruction, not an Arm A/Arm B replay comparison.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode, upstream rheological regularities, evidence needs and measurement objective before candidate ranking
execute read-only scientific tools, including the paper-derived state-aware rheology tool, external evidence retrieval, formulation inspection and process-state audits
rank experiment points according to scientific usefulness for the discovered material problem
try to falsify the provisional recommendation and test scientific interpretability, leakage and claim boundaries
adjudicate whether the proposed point remains useful under alternative evidence priorities, process-state uncertainty and the skeptic's strongest objections
resolve proposer, skeptic and robustness records and make the final pre-result decision
programmatically validate and freeze the recommendation with timestamp, hashes, model, candidate state, uncertainty and falsifiable acceptance criterion

deterministic_decision_diagnostics.intervention_sufficiency_rule: Decision order is: failure mode -> experiment intent -> required intervention-axis coverage -> evidence-supported candidates -> minimum sufficient intervention. For performance_mitigation, candidates covering EVERY independently supported axis (acrylic_like, minor_tackifier_like) are compared first. Minimum sufficient intervention is a tie-break WITHIN that group only. A candidate that zeroes an independently supported axis is a partial-coverage / mechanistic control, not the default performance rank-1; it must not become rank-1 merely because zeroing that axis lowers modifier burden.
deterministic_decision_diagnostics.note: These are transparent decision diagnostics, not fitted property predictions. Exact literature-anchor distance is retained only for audit and is not a primary ranking objective. Performance-mitigation and causal-isolation scenarios are separated so that single-factor attribution is not the default for every experiment.

acceptance_criterion.criterion: Across predeclared independent matched-process realizations, SI15-60 must be no greater than 0.20 and SI15-90 must be no greater than 0.30, both must be lower than the contemporaneous E2-core control and clearly below the E5 reference trajectory under the same protocol, and the 80-130 C response must remain monotonic. acceptance_criterion.failure_condition: Fail if either SI threshold is exceeded, if drift is not lower than the matched E2 control, if drift remains E5-like, if replicate variability prevents the predeclared comparison, if the temperature response leaves the 80-130 C supported domain, if required process/state records or calibration are missing, or if verified functionality and stoichiometry fall outside the prespecified limits.

judge_normalized.selection_rationale: The measured failure mode is thermal-hold instability: E5 has SI15-60 of 0.515 and SI15-90 of 0.931, versus 0.095 and 0.168 for E1. The experiment intent is performance_mitigation, so both independently supported intervention axes must remain active; a single-axis candidate such as S1C39 is therefore a control, not the primary mitigation experiment. Local experiments also show large E2 realization spread, so static viscosity or an uncalibrated temperature sweep cannot establish success. Paper-derived rheological rules require separate assessment of viscosity level, temperature response, temporal hold drift, and process/state calibration; the state-aware model supports a 120 C anchor but does not predict hold stability. Curated PUR literature supports acrylic-like modifiers as a coarse 15-25 wt% region and minor tackifier-like additions near 5 wt% and below about 10 wt%, but these are analogue priors rather than predictors of the held-out wet-lab result. S1C41 therefore tests 15 wt% acrylic-like modifier plus 5 wt% minor tackifier-like modifier on the E2 core: both axes are covered, the tackifier level is better supported than the 2.5 wt% level in S1C40, and the total burden is lower than higher-loading full-coverage alternatives. The Skeptic objection is resolved by acknowledging that S1C30 has lower burden but lies below the declared supported acrylic region, while S1C40 is not preferred because its tackifier level is a lower-bound extrapolation. The Robustness Adjudicator objection is resolved by selecting S1C41 rather than S1C40 and by making functionality verification, recalculated stoichiometry, matched process history, contemporaneous E2 control, replicate structure, and quantitative adjudication mandatory. This decision identifies an evidence-supported formulation region, not an exact optimum or exact-property prediction.

action_requests.reason: Required first to establish the paper-derived formulation-only versus state-aware structure, determine whether state calibration materially improves prediction, and identify whether the next experiment should emphasize viscosity level, temperature response, state calibration, or hold stability.

action_requests.reason: Retrieve the original low-drift reference trajectory and descriptors for comparison against candidate design objectives.

action_requests.reason: Retrieve the original high-drift reference trajectory and descriptors defining the established thermal-hold failure mode.

action_requests.name: get_repeatability_risk
action_requests.reason: Quantify the large observed run spread before treating the E2 anchor viscosity or temperature response as a stable material property.

action_requests.name: inspect_formulation
action_requests.reason: Document the reactive-core composition and separate chemistry-axis comparison from process-state variation before generating or comparing intervention candidates.

action_requests.name: get_temperature_support
action_requests.reason: Confirm the supported temperature domain and select any adjudication anchor only within the measured 80 to 130 C range.

action_requests.name: get_candidate_hypothesis
action_requests.reason: After the local objective is established, retrieve the evidence-derived candidate-space hypothesis, E2 anchor, independent acrylic-like and tackifier-like axes, and the historical claim boundary without treating it as a discovered optimum.

action_requests.name: query_external_priors
action_requests.reason: Obtain source-level chemistry priors only after identifying the local failure. Directly commensurate numeric anchors are limited; the available acrylic levels near 15 to 25 wt% and minor tackifier levels below about 10 wt% are directional or conservative design bounds, not exact local optima. Comparative stability evidence should be used to motivate modifier identity and functionality checks, not to claim a molecular mechanism.

candidate_evaluation_dimensions: Thermal-hold stability SI from 15 to 60 minutes and 15 to 90 minutes at 120 C
Absolute viscosity level at a predeclared anchor temperature within 80 to 130 C
Temperature-response shape and apparent sensitivity across the measured 80 to 130 C range
State calibration requirement and consistency with the state-aware master-curve structure
Repeatability across independent realization or process-history replicates
Preservation of the E2 reactive-core identity unless a bounded modifier intervention is selected
Acrylic-like modifier fraction and modifier functionality as separate chemistry axes where supported
Minor tackifier-like modifier fraction and family identity
Stoichiometric feasibility, reactive-group balance, processability, and extrapolation distance from measured or directly commensurate evidence
Evidence coverage and uncertainty penalty, including process-history and measurement uncertainty
counterfactual_checks: Would the candidate still be preferred if evaluated on hold-drift reduction rather than nominal viscosity alone?
Would the ranking change after accounting for the measured E2 repeatability spread?
Does the apparent improvement persist when temperature response is compared at matched state rather than nominal temperature only?
Is the proposed benefit attributable to the supported modifier axis, or could it arise from altered stoichiometry, catalyst content, preparation history, or thermal conditioning?
Would an E2-core-only control distinguish a modifier intervention from ordinary realization or process-state variation?
Does a combined acrylic-like and tackifier-like intervention remain within independently supported bounded regions rather than relying on an unsupported additive extrapolation?
Could the candidate pass a viscosity target while still reproducing the E5-like hot-hold failure?
Are all claims limited to rheological behavior and formulation-space evidence rather than an unverified molecular mechanism?
planner.decision_goal: Select one evidence-bounded formulation experiment intended to reduce thermal-hold viscosity drift while preserving an acceptable viscosity level and temperature response, with repeatability and process-state uncertainty measured explicitly.
design_implications: Use performance_mitigation rather than default single-factor causal isolation because thermal-hold drift is already an established failure mode.
Evaluate candidates on hold-stability drift as a primary objective, not only on nominal viscosity at one temperature.
Retain the E2 reactive core unless evidence supports a bounded formulation-family intervention.
A multi-component intervention is admissible if each modifier axis is independently supported and the combined levels remain within the bounded candidate lattice and stoichiometric constraints.
Use the state-shift master-curve and calibration findings to determine whether state calibration or matched process history is required before comparing candidates.
Use measured temperatures and the measured 15 to 90 minute hold window as the default domain; do not extrapolate unsupported temperatures or times.
Treat approximately 15 to 25 wt% acrylic-like modifier levels as external coarse directional anchors, not as an exact optimum.
Treat minor tackifier-like additions below about 10 wt% as a conservative evidence-bounded axis, not as proof of a required loading.
Preserve source units and do not infer a viscosity unit where the local payload leaves it unknown.
material_regularities_to_use: The measured E1, E2, and E3 temperature sweeps decrease monotonically from 80 to 130 C.
The temperature response is supported only over the measured 80 to 130 C range.
E1 and E5 show a strong contrast in thermal-hold drift at 120 C over the measured 15 to 90 minute window.
E2 exhibits large descriptive run-to-run spread across the temperature sweep, so an individual nominal viscosity should not be treated as a fully reproducible material property.
The original E2 formulation is the reactive-core anchor for candidate-space construction.
The distinction between thermal response and temporal hold drift must be preserved; a formulation with an acceptable temperature sweep can still fail during hot holding.
Process history, realization state, and stoichiometric consistency remain explicit uncertainty dimensions.
planner.physical_failure_mode: Thermal-hold instability is established by the original E5 profile, with SI increasing by 0.515 from 15 to 60 minutes and 0.931 from 15 to 90 minutes at 120 C, versus 0.095 and 0.168 for E1. The local system also has substantial realization or process-state uncertainty: E2 temperature-sweep repeatability has CV values of approximately 0.46 to 0.58 and max/min ratios of approximately 2.8 to 3.6. Therefore, nominal viscosity alone is not a sufficient design target.
required_measurements_for_adjudication: Temperature sweep from 80 to 130 C with the same measurement protocol and at least enough independent runs to quantify realization spread
Viscosity at a predeclared in-support anchor temperature, with source units preserved
Thermal-hold trajectory at 120 C over the measured 15 to 90 minute window, including SI at 15 to 60 and 15 to 90 minutes
Initial and held viscosity values sufficient to calculate SI without imputing missing values
Run-level records including process history, preparation timing, thermal conditioning, and stoichiometric quantities
State calibration or state-marker measurements if the upstream summary indicates that state shifts materially affect the master curve
Composition confirmation for acrylic-like and tackifier-like modifier fractions and relevant reactive functionality
Replicate measurements adequate to distinguish candidate effects from the observed E2 realization spread
uncertainty_triggers: The state-aware summary shows that state calibration is required but the candidate lacks a matched state measurement or process history.
Candidate temperature or hold time lies outside the measured 80 to 130 C and 15 to 90 minute domains.
Observed candidate drift is comparable to the E2 repeatability spread, preventing separation of intervention effect from realization noise.
A candidate relies on a literature percentage that is only directional or noncommensurate but is treated as an exact optimum.
Modifier functionality, molecular weight, catalyst environment, or MDI/polyol stoichiometry differs materially from the supporting evidence without a bounded rationale.
Initial viscosity is acceptable but thermal-hold drift is unmeasured or substantially uncertain.
Replicate runs disagree in a way that suggests process-history or state variation dominates chemistry.
The candidate requires an unverified change to reactive-core stoichiometry or exceeds the declared candidate-space bounds.

provisional_acceptance_criterion.claim: The candidate mitigates the established thermal-hold instability while retaining an interpretable in-support rheological response.
provisional_acceptance_criterion.criterion: Across independent matched-process replicates, SI15-60 should be no greater than 0.20 and SI15-90 should be no greater than 0.30, with both values clearly below the E5 reference trajectory and not explainable solely by E2-scale realization spread; the 80 to 130 C response must remain monotonic and the initial viscosity must be measurable without extrapolating outside the supported domain.
provisional_acceptance_criterion.failure_condition: Failure occurs if either drift criterion is exceeded, if drift is comparable to the E5-like failure trajectory, if replicate variability prevents separation from E2 realization noise, if the temperature response leaves the supported 80 to 130 C domain, or if state/process history is not sufficiently matched or calibrated.
provisional_acceptance_criterion.measurement_window: 120 C hold from 15 to 90 minutes, with SI15-60 and SI15-90; temperature sweep from 80 to 130 C

provisional_measurement_plan.primary_response: Thermal-hold viscosity drift at 120 C, quantified as SI from 15 to 60 minutes and from 15 to 90 minutes, with initial and held viscosity values recorded at run level; secondary responses are viscosity at a predeclared in-support anchor temperature and the full 80 to 130 C temperature-response curve.
provisional_measurement_plan.state_anchor_plan: Use the same mixing, reaction, thermal-conditioning, sample-age, and measurement history across candidates and E2 controls. Record process history and perform a state-specific viscosity anchor at 120 C before or at the start of the hold. Use replicate runs sufficient to distinguish candidate effects from the observed E2 realization spread; calibrate the state-aware master curve rather than comparing nominal viscosity alone.
provisional_measurement_plan.time_window: 15 to 90 minutes at 120 C, with mandatory SI calculations for 15 to 60 minutes and 15 to 90 minutes

regularities_used: Measured local evidence: E5 shows substantially greater thermal-hold drift than E1, with SI increasing by 0.515 from 15 to 60 minutes and 0.931 from 15 to 90 minutes versus 0.095 and 0.168 for E1.
Measured local evidence: E2 has large realization spread, with temperature-sweep CV values of approximately 0.46 to 0.58 and a maximum/minimum ratio up to approximately 3.57 at 120 C.
Measured local evidence: local temperature response is monotonically decreasing and supported only from 80 to 130 C.
Derived model rule: static viscosity, temperature response, and temporal hold drift are separate decision variables; viscosity alone cannot establish mitigation.
Derived model rule: a state-aware representation substantially improves transferability, with state-aware shared-shape R2 of approximately 0.998 versus formulation-only R2 of approximately 0.852.
Conservative design principle: for performance mitigation, both independently supported intervention axes must be covered before applying minimum sufficient intervention.

External analogue evidence: acrylic-like modifiers are supported as a coarse region around 15 to 25 wt%, with approximately 19 to 20 wt% directly commensurate in several analogue formulations and 15 wt% directional or noncommensurate evidence.

External analogue evidence: minor tackifier-like modifiers are supported around approximately 5 wt%, with a conservative upper region below about 10 wt%; these data support a family and bounded region, not an exact local optimum.

External comparative evidence: lower effective reactive-group density or lower-OH acrylic analogues showed lower viscosity rise than higher-OH analogues at comparable loading, but no local molecular mechanism is established.
Unresolved uncertainty: all candidate process-history fields are missing, and modifier functionality, stoichiometric contribution, and realization state must be verified.
proposer.scientific_target: Reduce thermal-hold viscosity drift while retaining an acceptable viscosity level and temperature-response shape, using the E2 reactive core as the formulation anchor and evaluating the intervention under matched process and realization conditions.
unresolved_questions: What are the verified reactive functionalities and effective stoichiometric contributions of AC1920 and TK100?
Does the candidate's apparent improvement persist after matched state calibration rather than nominal-temperature comparison?
How many independent realizations are required to resolve a candidate effect against the observed E2 CV of approximately 0.46 to 0.58?
Does the combined acrylic-like plus tackifier-like intervention improve hold stability without unacceptable changes in initial viscosity or temperature-response shape?
Is the useful design space a broad modifier family or a narrower region within approximately 15 to 25 wt% acrylic-like modifier and below about 10 wt% tackifier-like modifier?
Can the partial-coverage S1C39 control and a tackifier-only control be added later to separate axis contributions without replacing the full-coverage performance test?
Are the external numeric anchors sufficiently commensurate for the selected modifier identities, or should they remain directional priors only?

alternative_comparison.scientific_tradeoff: Lower total modifier burden than S1C41, but weaker support for the 2.5% tackifier level and greater dependence on extrapolation.
alternative_comparison.would_be_preferred_if: A conservative lower-bound tackifier probe below the repeated minor-resin cluster is explicitly acceptable and the goal is minimum perturbation rather than uniformly supported axis levels.

alternative_comparison.scientific_tradeoff: Lowest full-coverage burden, but its acrylic level is outside the stated 15-25% supported region and therefore is less robust when analogue-distance rewards are removed.
alternative_comparison.would_be_preferred_if: The declared acrylic evidence region is broadened to admit 10% acrylic-like modifier.

alternative_comparison.scientific_tradeoff: Cleaner attribution with strong acrylic support, but it does not test the complete performance-mitigation strategy because the tackifier axis is zeroed.
alternative_comparison.would_be_preferred_if: The objective changes to causal isolation of the acrylic-like axis.

required_conditions: Verify modifier functionality and reactive-group contributions, recalculate the true NCO:OH balance, and predefine allowable stoichiometric deviation.
Use a contemporaneous E2-core control prepared in the same batch or matched process sequence.
Prespecify independent realization count, replicate structure, variance handling, and numerical equivalence or superiority rules relative to E2 and E5.
Define mandatory process-history fields, matching tolerances, thermal-conditioning procedure, sample-age window, and deviation handling.
Retain the 80-130 C sweep, 120 C hold, SI15-60 and SI15-90 measurements, and state-anchor calibration; state explicitly that calibration does not itself establish hold-stability improvement.
Treat S1C41 as a bounded region test, not evidence of an exact optimum or molecular mechanism.

robustness_checks.detail: The proposal targets the established 120 C thermal-hold viscosity-drift failure rather than nominal viscosity alone, while retaining the E2 reactive core.
The Planner declares performance_mitigation, for which a dual-axis intervention is appropriate; causal attribution is not the primary claim.

S1C40 covers both axes but uses a 2.5% tackifier level below the repeated 4.8-6.4% evidence cluster. S1C41 covers both axes at 15% acrylic-like modifier and 5% tackifier-like modifier, both within the supported regions.

S1C40 is not demonstrably the minimum-burden full-coverage candidate because S1C30 has a lower 12.5% burden. However, S1C30 uses only 10% acrylic-like modifier, below the declared supported acrylic region of approximately 15-25%.

Removing exact analogue-distance rewards weakens S1C40 relative to S1C41 because its tackifier loading is a lower-bound extrapolation. S1C41 remains supported as a bounded region test, although the literature remains analogue evidence rather than a local optimum.

State-aware calibration and matched process history are correctly requested, but all candidates have high process-history uncertainty and the proposal lacks mandatory tolerances and a defined deviation rule.

The plan measures the required 80-130 C sweep and 120 C SI15-60/SI15-90 drift, but it does not prespecify replicate count, variance modeling, equivalence margins, or a quantitative comparison against E2 variability.

The Skeptic identified a serious ranking inconsistency and unresolved evidence-boundary issues sufficient to rerank, but not to abstain because a stronger full-coverage bounded candidate is available.

counterfactual_failures: If ranking is based on the primary failure mode plus evidence coverage and burden, S1C30 must be explicitly excluded or reconsidered before S1C40 can be called rank 1.
If the 15% acrylic point is treated as directional rather than directly commensurate, the evidence basis for S1C40 is weaker than the proposal's 'strong analogue' characterization implies.

If the tackifier axis is independently supported only from approximately 3% upward or approximately 4.8-6.4% in repeated examples, the 2.5% tackifier loading requires an explicitly labeled conservative extrapolation.
If candidate drift is comparable to E2 realization spread, the proposed acceptance rule may not identify mitigation without a prespecified replication and variance decision framework.

If the initial viscosity passes while SI fails, the plan correctly identifies failure conceptually, but the ranking rationale does not specify how such a result updates preference among S1C40, S1C45, and S1C50.

A one-point state calibration may align the temperature-response shape while leaving process-history-driven hold drift unresolved; matched-state comparison alone is not a sufficient stability control.

critical_findings.evidence: S1C30 is classified as full_coverage with 12.5% total modifier burden, whereas S1C40 is full_coverage with 17.5%. The proposal calls S1C40 the lowest-burden sufficient candidate without explaining why S1C30 is inadmissible beyond its lower analogue-support score and 10% acrylic level.
critical_findings.issue: The stated minimum-burden rationale for S1C40 is inconsistent with the supplied candidate diagnostics.

critical_findings.evidence: The 15% acrylic level is explicitly retained as provisional noncommensurate or directional evidence, while 2.5% tackifier is below the repeated external tackifier cluster of approximately 4.8-6.4% and below the broad stated region of 3-10%. The candidate is therefore a bounded hypothesis, not a fully independently anchored two-axis point.
critical_findings.issue: The selected modifier levels are not both directly commensurate evidence anchors.

critical_findings.evidence: The criterion requires drift to be 'not explainable solely by E2-scale realization spread' and says replicates must distinguish candidate effects, but it specifies neither the number of replicates, variance model, confidence rule, equivalence margin, nor decision procedure.
critical_findings.issue: The acceptance criterion contains an operationally vague comparison to E2-scale realization spread.

critical_findings.evidence: All candidates have six missing process fields and high process-history uncertainty. The plan requests records of mixing, reaction, conditioning, age, and timing but does not identify which fields are mandatory, allowable tolerances, or how deviations will invalidate or stratify a comparison.
critical_findings.issue: Matched process history is requested but not yet defined sufficiently to control the dominant uncertainty.

critical_findings.evidence: S1C40 changes acrylic-like and tackifier-like axes simultaneously. The proposer acknowledges unresolved two-axis attribution, but the primary experiment cannot determine whether either axis is necessary or whether an interaction drives the result.
critical_findings.issue: The combined intervention is appropriate for performance mitigation but does not support causal attribution of either modifier axis.

critical_findings.evidence: The proposal acknowledges that AC1920 and TK100 may contribute reactive functionality, while the E2 NCO:OH value applies only to the original reactive core. No verified functionality, recalculated NCO:OH balance, or predeclared stoichiometric tolerance is supplied.
critical_findings.issue: Stoichiometric and functionality uncertainty could make the nominal formulation differ materially from the intended intervention.

critical_findings.evidence: S1C40 is preferred over the lower-burden S1C30 partly because it lies in a 'strong_analogue_region' rather than a 'moderate_analogue_region,' even though exact analogue proximity is declared audit-only and the local hold outcome is unmeasured.
critical_findings.issue: The ranking may still be influenced by analogue-support category and literature-region proximity despite the stated nonuse of exact distance as a primary objective.

interpretability_failures: No explicit replicate count or prespecified statistical or equivalence rule is provided for distinguishing candidate drift from the observed E2 CV of approximately 0.46-0.58.
The plan does not clearly require a contemporaneous E2-core control prepared and measured under the same batch, operator, conditioning, and hold sequence.
The criterion that drift must be 'clearly below' E5 and 'not explainable solely' by E2 variability is insufficiently quantitative for adjudication.
Without verified modifier functionality and recalculated stoichiometry, an observed effect could reflect altered reactive-group balance rather than the intended acrylic-like or tackifier-like axis.
A state anchor at 120 C can calibrate viscosity scale and thermal-response shape but does not by itself establish or predict temporal hold stability.

leakage_check.detail: The supplied payload states that validation formulation identity and wet-lab hold results were unavailable, and the proposal does not cite a validation outcome or outcome-derived label. The use of the listed candidates and diagnostics is outcome-blind in the supplied record. However, the payload notes that the exact V2 grid and fine-refinement software were formalized after validation, so provenance of the operational candidate grid should remain documented separately from leakage of validation results.

regularity_alignment.detail: The proposal correctly prioritizes thermal-hold drift, uses the performance-mitigation intent, retains the E2 core, covers both independently identified intervention axes, and includes state-aware calibration. However, the claim that S1C40 has the lowest total modifier burden among sufficient full-coverage candidates is not supported by the scorecards: S1C30 is also classified as full coverage with a lower 12.5% total burden. In addition, S1C40 uses a 15% acrylic level described as directional/noncommensurate and a 2.5% tackifier level below the repeatedly documented 4.8-6.4% cluster, so its evidence support is not uniformly strong.

required_corrections: Reconcile S1C40 against S1C30 using a transparent admissibility rule: either exclude S1C30 because 10% acrylic is outside the declared supported band, or acknowledge that S1C40 is not the minimum-burden full-coverage candidate.
State explicitly that 15% acrylic and 2.5% tackifier are conservative design extrapolations or lower-bound probes rather than directly commensurate local optima.
Specify verified modifier functionality, reactive-group contribution, recalculated NCO:OH balance, and allowable stoichiometric deviation before execution.
Define mandatory process-history fields, matching tolerances, thermal-conditioning procedure, sample-age window, and handling of deviations.
Add a contemporaneous E2-core control and predeclare the number of independent realizations, replicate structure, and statistical or equivalence rule for comparison against E2 variability.

Replace vague acceptance language such as 'clearly below' and 'not explainable solely' with numerical margins and a prespecified adjudication method while retaining SI15-60 and SI15-90 as primary responses.
Preserve the state-anchor measurement, but explicitly state that it calibrates viscosity scale and temperature response and is not evidence of hold-stability improvement.

scientific_boundary_check.detail: The proposal generally respects the boundaries between local measured evidence, state-aware rheological modeling, and external analogue evidence. It does not claim a molecular mechanism or treat static viscosity as thermal-hold stability. Qualification is required because the minimum-burden claim is contradicted by S1C30, the selected 15% and 2.5% levels are not uniformly directly commensurate anchors, and the conservative decision rule is reconstructed rather than a directly measured literature fact.

design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

PAT_US20070155859A1: tackifiers/rheology-control agents typically used below about 10 wt%
minor_tackifier_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 5% represents the repeatedly documented minor-resin region and 10% is a conservative coarse upper level.

result.claim_boundary: External examples are analogues. They support candidate-family and coarse-region hypotheses, not an exact optimum for AC1920/TK100 and not a proven local molecular mechanism. The current reconstruction uses only pre-result evidence at runtime; the exact validation coordinates and outcome are excluded from candidate construction, ranking and tie-breaking.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

minor_tackifier_like.basis: Curated PUR examples repeatedly place tackifying/hydrocarbon resin near 5%, with broader guidance below about 10%.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement software are later reproducible operationalizations of the evidence-constrained region and are not represented as the original contemporaneous freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.

local_reactive_core_anchor.reason: E2 is the geometric centre of the original five-point local design: 50/50 PPG2000/PDP-70 and NCO:OH=1.80, centered between E1/E3 stoichiometric perturbations and E4/E5 composition perturbations.
local_reactive_core_anchor.stoichiometry_note: The E2 NCO:OH=1.80 label applies to the original reactive core. If a modifier contributes reactive OH or another NCO-reactive group, true stoichiometry must be recalculated from verified material specifications.

stability_hypotheses.H1_formulation_family: Partial replacement of the reactive-only formulation by an acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like resin can reduce hot-hold viscosity drift under matched process conditions.
stability_hypotheses.H2_functionality: At comparable acrylic loading, lower effective reactive-group density or lower-OH acrylic chemistry is expected to be more favorable for hot-hold viscosity stability than more highly reactive acrylic chemistry.
stability_hypotheses.H3_region: A useful candidate region is expected within the externally supported coarse space spanned by 15-25% acrylic-like modifier and 0-10% minor tackifier-like modifier, while preserving the relative E2 reactive-core proportions.

tool_trace.name: query_external_priors
tool_trace.reason: Obtain source-level chemistry priors only after identifying the local failure. Directly commensurate numeric anchors are limited; the available acrylic levels near 15 to 25 wt% and minor tackifier levels below about 10 wt% are directional or conservative design bounds, not exact local optima. Comparative stability evidence should be used to motivate modifier identity and functionality checks, not to claim a molecular mechanism.
